interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines state that a PI-RADS score of 5 mandates a repeat biopsy to confirm histological progression before a change in treatment strategy. The guideline requires that a repeat biopsy be performed when a lesion is identified on MRI to confirm histological progression.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, I disagree with the suggestion of biopsy because the guideline makes the decision decisive based on the PI-RADS 5 finding.
EXPERT-COHORT, I disagree with the deferral because the criterion states that the next step is staging and treatment when there is a tissue diagnosis, which is the case here.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: Positive means the guideline suggests staging and treatment, not more tissue.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does.
psa_trend - the PSA velocity: 38.28 ng/mL/yr means the guideline requires consideration of progression.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: 3.26 ng/mL² is a value that must be considered in risk stratification.

interventions.speaker: MODERATOR
interventions.who: chairs the discussion; sets the open questions and assigns the documents
interventions.body:
This case is highly conflicted between the EAU guideline requiring a repeat biopsy for PI-RADS 5 and the cohort criterion suggesting deferral due to prior biopsy status.

The documents for this session were fixed by EXPERT-TRACE; what I add is the question each one has to answer, and the open questions for the room.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> Determine if the lesion is compared against an earlier study to inform the need for repeat biopsy.
  psa_trend (get_psa_trend) -> Determine if the PSA velocity indicates progression that warrants further action.
  previous_notes (get_previous_notes) -> Determine the grade (Gleason/ISUP) and details of the prior positive biopsy and current surveillance plan.

OPEN QUESTIONS for this conference — these are what the decision hangs on:
  Q1. Does the radiology_report indicate whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study?
  Q2. Does the psa_trend indicate progression that warrants further action beyond the initial decision?

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 187.00 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 13 months; velocity +156.30 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 4 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 632.9 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 181.6-2206.0.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: NO BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.48
  uncertainty  +/- 0.17 epistemic (95% band 0.16-0.81), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  LOW ('discuss' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 59% of the time over the 29 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address the moderator's questions.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The panel protocol concluded NO BIOPSY based on the cohort criterion (PSA $\ge 20$ ng/mL), which was supported by the retrieved data.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. Does the radiology_report indicate whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study? The report states "COMPARISON: new," indicating the lesion is not compared against an earlier study.
Q2. Does the psa_trend indicate progression that warrants further action beyond the initial decision? The PSA trend shows a rise to 187.0 ng/mL, with a velocity of 38.28 ng/mL/yr, which supports the need for further action.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PSA velocity (38.28 ng/mL/yr) is highly relevant as it indicates progression, which is a key factor in the EAU guideline consideration. The prior positive biopsy status is also critical as it informs the cohort criterion used by the panel.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
Given the conflict between the EAU guideline (PI-RADS 5 mandates repeat biopsy) and the cohort criterion (prior positive biopsy suggests deferral), the rising PSA velocity supports further investigation, but the prior biopsy status weighs against immediate re-biopsy. I suggest deferral pending further discussion on staging and treatment planning, as per the panel's current position.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: defer | MISSING: none
